name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog:
Playback start speed and reliability. PlaybackInfo metadata is now cached for 5 minutes instead of 15 seconds, removing a full WAN round trip from nearly every press of play; the metadata/token calls made before playback are bounded at 20 seconds (a hung remote used to stall play for up to 5 minutes); the relay buffer grew 80KB to 256KB; and old-version friends stop paying a wasted round trip per play.

Streaming reliability: a remote server restarting used to break playback for up to 5 hours because this side kept re-sending a session token the remote had forgotten. The stream handler now detects the rejection, drops the dead token, mints a fresh one and retries once. WAN bandwidth measurement is also fixed (it silently failed against current-version friends since the token rewrite, so bitrate caps stopped applying - constant buffering on slower links); remotes now serve it through a token-authenticated Peer/BitrateTest route.

Cleanup: deleting a library mapping from settings now removes its federated items, library and cache entries instead of orphaning them forever; unfriending clears pool rosters and static caches, and revokes outstanding playback tokens immediately instead of up to 24 hours later; uninstalling revokes the plugin's internal relay API key from Jellyfin's key store and deletes a custom-path cache file; and a one-time sweep removes relay keys orphaned by the pre-0.0.77 save bug.

The Federation settings page was redesigned to match Jellyfin's native dashboard look: grouped sections, plain-language help text, confirmations on destructive actions, no custom theme-breaking styling.

219 tests. Smaller known issues are listed in KNOWN_ISSUES.md.
